FisherKing Image Factory v2.0

What's New in v2.0

Image Factory v2.0 introduces a major architectural redesign focused on modularity, scalability, and maintainability while preserving the original philosophy:

One Prompt • One Model • One Seed → Multiple Creative Directions

This release transforms Image Factory into a cleaner, more extensible framework while remaining fully compatible with its original workflow.

✨ New Features
✓ Wireless Prompt Conditioning
Positive and negative conditioning are now distributed wirelessly throughout the workflow.
Variants automatically inherit Engine conditioning without manual wiring.
✓ Independent Variant Modules

Each creative variant now operates as a completely self-contained pipeline with its own:

Prompt Override
Negative Override
LoRA Stack
Sampler Configuration
CFG / Steps
Denoise Settings
Independent Save Pipeline
✓ LoRA Isolation
Fixed previous cross-variant LoRA routing issues.
Every variant now functions independently without affecting other creative branches.
✓ Improved Workflow Architecture
Cleaner separation between the IF Engine and Variant modules.
Simplified workflow expansion.
Reduced node clutter.
Easier maintenance and future enhancements.
✓ Optional Post Processing
Optional wireless upscaling path.
Disabled by default.
Can be enabled when higher resolution output is desired.
✓ Baseline Output

Generate a clean reference image without LoRAs, making it easy to compare every creative variant against the original generation.

Core Philosophy

Image Factory is designed around controlled creative exploration.

Every variant begins with the same Engine state while applying its own artistic interpretation.

This enables meaningful comparisons between:

Prompt Engineering
LoRA Combinations
Artistic Styles
Creative Variants

without introducing unnecessary randomness.

The IF Engine manages all shared resources used by every creative branch.

Performance Note

This workflow prioritizes modularity and creative comparison rather than maximum generation speed. Generation time will vary depending on your hardware, selected model, number of active variants, and LoRAs.
